acceptance: Fork-owned contract records version, fork/upstream SHA, exact wheel checksum and canonical producer run/attempt/artifact provenance; core can consume it with read-only access and no fork-write token.

A delivery is never marked verified before all required trusted fork checks and clean distribution verification pass on the actual merged main SHA; skipped/missing/failed/wrong-publisher checks refuse in the fork.
The producer verifies source/build/relocation/runtime/distribution integrity itself using existing build and test capabilities; no duplicate verifier or fork suite is required in core.
Actual canonical artifact replay and installed fork-wheel proof exercised; wrong run/head/attempt/digest/provenance and expired artifact refuse with actionable fork-owned recovery evidence.
No public package/release, parallel normal build, registry service, Theseus modification or core orchestration is introduced; fork PR passes its ordinary review/protection/CI and merges.
A schema-versioned verified record retains one version-to-wheel-hash binding; same-version/different-hash delivery is refused in the fork and is not published as a tooling-only update.

Expiry recovery reruns the same canonical source SHA, passes fork-required checks and emits a new verified attempt with identical version/hash binding; consumed receipt evidence remains verifiable after payload expiry.

description:
Implement in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot, not core or Theseus. Own a reliable verified wheel delivery contract using existing downstream build/verify tooling and canonical source/package/engine CI. State the minimum schema-versioned consumer contract: version, full fork/upstream identities, wheel filename+SHA256, trusted canonical producer workflow/run/attempt/artifact identity and links to fork validation evidence. Only expose a verified delivery once ALL fork-required trusted checks and clean distribution verification pass at the actual merged main SHA. Reuse that exact build, never PR-synthetic or arbitrary latest-main bytes. Source-to-wheel/relocation verification and fork runtime semantics are producer responsibilities.

Decision gates: select existing GitHub Actions artifact transport rather than a new registry/service/database/public release; prove the completion record is trusted producer output, not self-reported candidate metadata, and that a core read-only consumer can retrieve it. Missing/expired artifact becomes a fork issue naming the exact canonical run to recover. No alternate unbound automatic rebuild. Core receives a trustworthy product contract and does not recompute fork required-check membership or source verification. No SQLGlot changes or new API in Theseus. Keep the producer disabled until its own checks/access/identity are proven; no core-only reliability dependency blocks implementation.

One delivered version maps to one wheel hash: retain that binding in verifiable producer delivery evidence and reject any later different hash for the same version, including tooling-only main builds. A changed product requires a new fork version. Consumer receipt evidence must remain verifiable after a core PR carries the bytes. Artifact-expiry recovery is a fork rerun of the canonical producer at the same merged SHA, all required checks passing again, and a newly verified exact attempt/record; it is not acceptance of an old mismatched attempt or an alternate build. Preserve version/hash immutability during recovery. Core-reviewed configuration, not record-controlled fields, fixes trusted producer repository, workflow path, ref and event.
